conf.description: cisco-asa connection-events dataset, syslog-raw format (RFC 3164 free-text 302013/302014/302015/302016/302020/302021 Built/Teardown messages): parsing is deferred entirely to the Elastic cisco_asa integration, which branches on the parsed message ID and applies its own per-ID grok/dissect. This pipeline is intentionally thin: it only tags event.dataset and passes _raw through untouched.

conf.comment: cisco-asa / connection-events / syslog-raw: free-text Built/Teardown sentences whose token order is positional per message template (302013/302015 differ from 302014/302016). Do NOT re-grok source/destination sockets, direction, bytes, duration, or interface names here -- the Elastic cisco_asa integration ships the per-message-ID grok/dissect for this exact family and lands cisco.asa.* plus ECS fields from _raw. Re-implementing that parsing in Cribl would fight the integration and risk duplicate or conflicting fields. Every field-table transform in this dataset (message_id lookup, protocol case-fold, duration-to-nanoseconds) requires a field already extracted from the body, so none of them are safely implementable pre-parse; they are left to the integration's stock pipeline / a downstream @custom pipeline per the map's elastic recommendation.

functions.description: document why this pipeline does not parse _raw
tag the event with its dataset ahead of the Elastic integration's own parsing of _raw
